KEY MESSAGE 1...A cold front will yield a round of showers Fri 
evening, followed by drier, cooler and blustery weather Saturday.

A vigorous short wave moving across VA this afternoon and will 
rotate northeast across SNE 21z-03z, resulting in a period of 
widespread showers for MA/RI/CT this evening. Behind this feature, 
dry weather overspreads the region later this evening into Sat. 

Temperature-wise, weak CAA advects across the region overnight 
behind departing short wave, bringing an end to our mild weather 
from this afternoon across eastern CT-RI and southeast MA. However, 
the CAA is weak so temps will still remain slightly above normal, 
with lows in the upper 30s to lower 40s tonight and mainly in the 
30s Sat night, although feeling cooler give blustery west winds 10-
20 mph, except up to 35 mph Cape Cod and islands. Highs Saturday 
will climb into the upper 40s and lower 50s, a few degs above 
normal, however it will feel cooler given the blustery west winds 15-
25 mph. Given the cyclonic flow Saturday, along with additional 
short wave energy pivoting through the upper flow, expecting more 
clouds than sunshine Saturday, followed by a low prob of a few 
showers in the evening, especially across Northern MA. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Frontal system brings another period of steady 
rainfall Monday, followed by gusty and potentially strong northwest 
winds Monday night.

The next storm system to affect Southern New England is a frontal 
system which treks eastward from the Ohio Valley and 
central/northern Appalachians early Monday morning, pulling away 
from Southern New England into the Gulf of Maine late Monday and/or 
Monday evening. Primary sfc low begins to occlude with possible 
energy transfer to a secondary low pressure development along the 
frontal boundary near the lower Hudson Valley early Monday morning. 
The strength of this secondary low and how progressive it is - were 
it to develop - is still a bit uncertain, but will certainly drive 
the impacts we'll see. These alternate potential outcomes are shown 
in ensemble cluster analyses, with two primary clusters by 00z 
Tuesday either (1) a weaker, more progressive secondary low that 
closes off into Nova Scotia, supported by majority of EPS/AIFS 
ensemble members or (2) a stronger, slower secondary low that closes 
off as it nears the mouth of the Merrimack River, a solution cluster 
supported by EPS and GEFS members. Monday does look like a washout 
with at least blustery northwesterly post-frontal northwest winds. 
If the stronger and slower secondary low were to materialize, we 
could see somewhat higher rain totals but also a stronger surge in 
northwest winds post-frontal - potentially supportive of wind 
headlines in the favored NW flow areas around the hills of Worcester 
County and the Berkshires and also potential for gale or strong-gale 
force northwesterly gusts. This latter outcome is best shown by the 
00z/27th ECMWF operational run, which shows 925 mb NW winds of 40-45 
kt and 850 mb NW winds upwards of 60 kt in the cold advection, and 
there are 20-40% probs of 10-m wind gusts 50+ kt Monday evening 
around the interior high terrain. 

We'll have to watch the strength of the 500 mb trough and how 
quickly it becomes negatively tilted before we get a better handle 
on which solution is closer to reality. As it stands right now, 
Monday does look to be a washout and rain could be enough to cause 
some within-bank rises on rivers, but the main impact may end up 
being a period of stronger post-frontal northwest winds as colder 
air pours in behind the system.
  
KEY MESSAGE 3...Drier and blustery but with seasonable 
temperatures through midweek, then a warming trend by late in 
the week. 

Deamplifying, quasi-zonal flow aloft takes hold behind the 
Monday/Monday night storm system. Strong high pressure takes hold of 
the mid-Atlantic/northern Appalachians by Tuesday, with initial 
period of seasonably cool temperatures to open the month of 
December. Expect dry but blustery weather through midweek...and 
although temperature profiles are cool, high and low temperatures 
still look around seasonable in the mid 40s, though it'll feel 
cooler with the northwest breezes. By late in the week, high 
pressure moves offshore allowing for a steady warming trend, and 
highs could return back into the upper 50s, perhaps near 60, which 
would be some 10 degrees above normal.
